description:
Maximize validated production CPU throughput on the Ryzen 9 5900X by measuring and closing AVX2-era kernel, decoder, and dispatch gaps against the strongest compatible open-source implementations.

## Background

The target is the observed Zen 3 host with AVX2, PCLMULQDQ, YMM VPCLMULQDQ, POPCNT, BMI1 and BMI2. Hardware-specific optimization preserves portable scalar fallback and the existing mathematical and coding contracts. Profiling distinguishes kernel limitations from representation, allocation, dispatch and memory-traffic costs. The competitive objective applies to a frozen, justified workload set, not a claim of a universal hardware optimum.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Provide a shared versioned protocol and independent family surveys and consumer profiles satisfying the [measurement contract](dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/measurement-contract.md). Numeric settings and cell addenda are frozen before confirmation, with exploratory pilots excluded and independent holdout evidence retained.

- [hard] REQ-02: Deliver measured outcomes for raw carry-less multiplication dispatch and polynomial crossovers, consumer-driven $\mathrm{GF}(2^8)$ feasibility, bit reductions, transpose/bitslice conversion, logical buffers and profiled shift/permutation consumers. Production selection includes only qualifying candidates; a field feasibility study may conclude that no byte-region API or packing redesign is justified.

- [hard] REQ-03: Deliver a profiled, allocation-free steady-state min-sum path and reusable SIMD batch decoding with per-frame convergence and partial batches under the declared deterministic numerical contract. Complete a mandatory bounded exploration/decision checkpoint for quantized, layered and QC-aware LDPC; ship such candidates only with reviewed contracts and qualifying throughput/latency/BER/FER evidence. Compare matched-algorithm and fastest quality-compatible measured decoders separately, including AFF3CT and applicable surveyed NR/DVB implementations.

- [hard] REQ-04: Select measured winners and crossover boundaries through the canonical offline tuning system and verify actual production dispatch. Record conservative portable, tuned portable and native-build results separately; unknown hosts retain deterministic safe fallback.

- [hard] REQ-05: Publish a reproducible final competitive scorecard with per-workload throughput, latency, scaling and uncertainty, plus assembly/profiler attribution of all material remaining gaps. Reprofile after integration and give each residual gap a measured limit, preserved no-win result, or concrete tracked follow-up; thresholds and stopping rules are frozen before trials.

- [hard] REQ-06: Preserve shared mathematical and standards conformance, zero tail padding, Rust 1.95 compatibility, unsafe-kernel isolation, canonical library abstractions and deterministic seeded execution. Decoder precision or schedule changes require a separately reviewed numerical contract and BER/FER evidence with sample counts and confidence intervals.

- [aspirational] REQ-07: Meet or exceed the fastest compatible measured open-source implementation on each primary workload cell, with the outcome and uncertainty reported even when the target is falsified.

## Notes

Implementation work is CPU-focused; AVX-512, GFNI and GPU kernel expansion do not accelerate the target host. Correctness, mandatory benchmarking and honest reporting are hard requirements. External implementations remain benchmark comparators; this epic does not authorize new production dependencies on them.
